1.3.1.3-r1.burton_quote: There is not one cause of this melancholy, nor one humour which begets it, but diverse diversely intermixed, from whence proceeds this variety of Symptoms

1.3.1.3-r10.burton_quote: are usually sad and solitary, and that continually, and in excess, more than ordinary suspicious, more fearful, and have long, sore, and most corrupt imaginations

1.3.1.3-r11.burton_quote: they will endure no company, they dream of graves still, and dead men, and think themselves bewitched or dead

1.3.1.3-r12.burton_quote: see and talk with black men, and converse familiarly with devils
1.3.1.3-r12.translation: and hanged men and dead men

1.3.1.3-r13.burton_quote: that thought every night she had to do with the devil

1.3.1.3-r14.burton_quote: had a black man in the likeness of a Soldier, still following him wheresoever he was

1.3.1.3-r15.burton_quote: would imitate most of their voices
1.3.1.3-r15.translation: A certain baron mimics the lowing of oxen and the braying of asses

1.3.1.3-r16.burton_quote: that thought himself and everything else he had, great: great wife, great horses, could not abide little things, but would have great pots to drink in, great hose, and great shoes bigger than his feet

1.3.1.3-r2.burton_quote: Cold melancholy (saith Benedic. Victorius Faventinus pract. mag.) is a cause of dotage, and more mild Symptoms, if hot or more adust, or more violent passions, and furies

1.3.1.3-r3.burton_quote: with what kind of Melancholy every one is troubled, for it much avails to know it; one is enraged by fervent heat, another is possessed by sad and cold; one is fearful, shamefast; the other impudent and bold

1.3.1.3-r4.burton_quote: they see or hear plays, dancing, and such-like sports
1.3.1.3-r4.translation: The patient laughs, if it comes from the blood; ... hear music

1.3.1.3-r5.burton_quote: That being by chance at a sermon, saw a woman fall off from a form half asleep, at which object most of the company laughed, but he for his part, was so much moved, that for three whole days after

1.3.1.3-r6.burton_quote: of a great wit, and excellently learned

1.3.1.3-r8.burton_quote: they sleep little, their urine is subtle and fiery

1.3.1.3-r9.burton_quote: This humour, saith he, prepares them to endure death itself, and all manner of torments with invincible courage, and ’tis a wonder to see with what alacrity they will undergo such tortures
1.3.1.3-r9.translation: Swept away by fury, they are driven to commit these deeds; ... and as their fury grows sharper they grow bolder, and are only the more provoked by punishments
